 - If your command will create new directories or files, first use this tool to run `ls` to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location.
 - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes in your command (e.g., cd "path with spaces/file.txt")
 - Try to maintain your current working directory throughout the session by using absolute paths and avoiding usage of `cd`. You may use `cd` if the User explicitly requests it. In particular, never prepend `cd <current-directory>` to a `git` command — `git` already operates on the current working tree, and the compound triggers a permission prompt.
 - You may specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). By default, your command will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
 - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. You do not need to use '&' at the end of the command when using this parameter.
 - For git commands:
  - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
  - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
  - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.
 - Avoid unnecessary `sleep` commands:
  - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
  - Use the Monitor tool to stream events from a background process (each stdout line is a notification). For one-shot "wait until done," use Bash with run_in_background instead.
  - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — use `run_in_background`. No sleep needed.
  - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause.
  - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
  - Long leading `sleep` commands are blocked. To poll until a condition is met, use Monitor with an until-loop (e.g. `until <check>; do sleep 2; done`) — you get a notification when the loop exits. Do not chain shorter sleeps to work around the block.
 - When running `find`, search from `.` (or a specific path), not `/` — scanning the full filesystem can exhaust system resources on large trees.
 - When using `find -regex` with alternation, put the longest alternative first. Example: use `'.*\.\(tsx\|ts\)'` not `'.*\.\(ts\|tsx\)'` — the second form silently skips `.tsx` files.


# Committing changes with git

Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:

You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. The numbered steps below indicate which commands should be batched in parallel.

Git Safety Protocol:
- NEVER update the git config
- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions 
- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it
- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it
- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit
- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries
- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the Bash tool:
  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.
  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.
  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.
2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:
  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).
  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files
  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"
  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area.
   - Create the commit with a message, ending with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.
   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.
4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook: fix the issue and create a NEW commit

Important notes:
- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands
- NEVER use the TodoWrite or Agent tools
- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so
- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.
- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.
- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit
- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:
<example>
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   Commit message here.
   EOF
   )"
</example>

# Creating pull requests
Use the gh command via the Bash tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.

IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel using the Bash tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:
   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)
   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed
   - Check if the current branch tracks a remote branch and is up to date with the remote, so you know if you need to push to the remote
   - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch)
2. Analyze all changes that will be included in the pull request, making sure to look at all relevant commits (NOT just the latest commit, but ALL commits that will be included in the pull request!!!), and draft a pull request title and summary:
   - Keep the PR title short (under 70 characters)
   - Use the description/body for details, not the title
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Create new branch if needed
   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed
   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting. End the body with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
<example>
gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

## Test plan
[Bulleted markdown checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]
EOF
)"
</example>

Important:
- DO NOT use the TodoWrite or Agent tools
- Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it

# Other common operations
- View comments on a Github PR: gh api repos/foo/bar/pulls/123/comments

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacements in files.

Usage:
- You must use your `Read` tool at least once in the conversation before editing. This tool will error if you attempt an edit without reading the file.
- When editing text from Read tool output, ensure you preserve the exact indentation (tabs/spaces) as it appears AFTER the line number prefix. The line number prefix format is: line number + tab. Everything after that is the actual file content to match. Never include any part of the line number prefix in the old_string or new_string.
- ALWAYS prefer editing existing files in the codebase. NEVER write new files unless explicitly required.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid adding emojis to files unless asked.
- The edit will FAIL if `old_string` is not unique in the file. Either provide a larger string with more surrounding context to make it unique or use `replace_all` to change every instance of `old_string`.
- Use `replace_all` for replacing and renaming strings across the file. This parameter is useful if you want to rename a variable for instance.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

# Build New Preview Workflow

**Goal:** Turn user intent into a hardened, reviewable artifact.

**CRITICAL:** If a step directs you to another snapshot file, read it fully and follow it. No exceptions.

Subagents, when the capability is available, are an important part of this workflow. Use them as directed by the workflow steps.
If you need an explicit user instruction to run them, ask once now for the whole workflow run.

## READY FOR DEVELOPMENT STANDARD

A specification is "Ready for Development" when:

- **Actionable**: Every task has a file path and specific action.
- **Logical**: Tasks ordered by dependency.
- **Testable**: All ACs use Given/When/Then.
- **Complete**: No placeholders or TBDs.
- **Sufficient**: No known requirement, acceptance, dependency, or implementation gaps remain unresolved.
- **Coherent**: No unresolved ambiguities or internal contradictions.

## SCOPE STANDARD

A specification should target a **single user-facing goal** within **900–1600 tokens**:

- **Single goal**: One cohesive feature, even if it spans multiple layers/files. Multi-goal means >=2 **top-level independent shippable deliverables** — each could be reviewed, tested, and merged as a separate PR without breaking the others. Never count surface verbs, "and" conjunctions, or noun phrases. Never split cross-layer implementation details inside one user goal.
  - Split: "add dark mode toggle AND refactor auth to JWT AND build admin dashboard"
  - Don't split: "add validation and display errors" / "support drag-and-drop AND paste AND retry"
- **900–1600 tokens**: Optimal range for LLM consumption. Below 900 risks ambiguity; above 1600 risks context-rot in implementation agents.
- **Neither limit is a gate.** Both are proposals with user override.

## Conventions

- Every operational cross-file reference in this workflow is an absolute snapshot path. Open it directly; do not resolve it relative to a skill directory.
- `{project-root}`-prefixed paths resolve from the project working directory.
- Whenever this workflow captures or records a version-control revision, obtain the full canonical identifier directly from version control and preserve it verbatim.

## On Activation

### Step 1: Execute Prepend Steps

Execute each of these steps in order before proceeding (`_None._` means skip):

_None._

### Step 2: Load Persistent Facts

Treat every entry below as foundational context you carry for the rest of the workflow run. Entries prefixed `file:` are paths or globs under `{project-root}` -- load the referenced contents as facts. All other entries are facts verbatim (`_None._` means none):

- file:{project-root}/**/project-context.md

### Step 3: Execute Append Steps

Execute each of these steps in order (`_None._` means skip):

_None._

## WORKFLOW ARCHITECTURE

This uses **step-file architecture** for disciplined execution:

- **Micro-file Design**: Each step is self-contained and followed exactly
- **Just-In-Time Loading**: Only load the current step file
- **Sequential Enforcement**: Complete steps in order, no skipping
- **State Tracking**: Persist progress via spec frontmatter and in-memory variables
- **Append-Only Building**: Build artifacts incrementally

### Step Processing Rules

1. **READ COMPLETELY**: Read the entire step file before acting
2. **FOLLOW SEQUENCE**: Execute sections in order
3. **WAIT FOR INPUT**: Halt at checkpoints and wait for human
4. **LOAD NEXT**: When directed, read fully and follow the next step file

### Critical Rules (NO EXCEPTIONS)

- **NEVER** load multiple step files simultaneously
- **ALWAYS** read entire step file before execution
- **NEVER** skip steps or optimize the sequence
- **ALWAYS** follow the exact instructions in the step file
- **ALWAYS** halt at checkpoints and wait for human input

Users come away able to create an account, log in, stay logged in across restarts, recover gracefully if their session expires mid-use, and navigate the whole app shell even though most feature screens are still placeholders.
8	
9	## Stories
10	
11	- Story 1.1: Project Scaffold, Stack Integration & Core Infrastructure
12	- Story 1.2: Design Token System & Core Component Library
13	- Story 1.3: Account Creation and Login
14	- Story 1.4: Silent Session Refresh & Persistence
15	- Story 1.5: Expired-Session Recovery Overlay
16	- Story 1.6: Base Navigation Shell with Feature Placeholders

18	## Requirements & Constraints
19	
20	- Account creation and login round-trip through the backend with exactly two fields (email, password) — no password confirmation, no display-name field at signup. Login/signup/refresh are the only calls using the anon key; every other call uses the user's access token.
21	- A valid, unexpired session must persist across app restarts with no re-prompt; nearing/past-expiry sessions refresh silently with no visible loading UI unless the call exceeds 300ms.
22	- When the backend reports an expired session, an overlay appears over whatever screen is active (never a navigation away); the underlying screen's state/scroll position is preserved; "Entrar novamente" leads to biometric/PIN re-auth, not a login form.
23	- All four base destinations (Home/Chat, side menu, Meus Registros, Configurações) must be reachable from launch; any destination whose feature isn't built yet shows a visually distinct, fully-polished placeholder — never a broken link and never a visibly "unfinished" look.
24	- Local UI interactions must respond in <100ms; any network call >300ms shows a loading indicator (manual timing spot-check, no automated perf tooling).
25	- Zero Clean Architecture layer violations: domain imports neither Flutter nor anything from a data layer.
26	- ≥80% domain-layer test coverage; the write-failure matrix (5 write endpoints × 3 failure types: timeout, malformed response, no connection = 15 scenarios) must be fully handled with zero unhandled exceptions — this epic builds the one shared, reusable test helper every later feature's write-endpoint tests reuse.
27	- Zero hardcoded visual values outside the design-tokens file; every control must honor Dynamic Type without truncating.
28	- An integration spike, before any other building, must prove `dio` + `flutter_secure_storage` + `get_it` work together in one bootstrap — this combination is otherwise unverified.
29	
30	## Technical Decisions
31	
32	- Single DI container: exactly one `get_it` instance registered at bootstrap; `dio` is configured through it; secrets (`FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`) load via `flutter_dotenv` from a gitignored `.env`, never hardcoded.
33	- One sealed `Failure` hierarchy, exactly 14 subtypes (13 from the backend's error taxonomy plus a local-only `MalformedResponse`), defined once and never redefined/subset per feature; every repository method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (or a `Stream` for SSE), with no native/dio exception ever escaping unmapped.
34	- One retry interceptor on the `dio`/`ApiClient` layer retries only the 6 server-marked `retryable:true` codes; every other failure surfaces once, unretried.
35	- One URL builder maps every operation to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path-params>` (never the literal OpenAPI REST path); one interceptor owns headers — `apikey` on every call, anon-key bearer token only on signup/login/refresh, user access token on everything else.
36	- Exactly one `SessionStatus` stream is exposed from the auth feature's domain layer and registered once in DI as a singleton; every later consumer (including RF07/Epic 4) injects/listens to it rather than re-deriving session validity from a raw 401 or a second stream.
37	- This epic builds the `go_router` redirect skeleton composing session state; Epic 2 (RF03) later plugs a local vault-status gate into the same redirect, checked before session status — this epic should leave that composition point open rather than hardcoding a session-only redirect.
38	- Strict layer direction applies project-wide: only `data/` imports `dio`/`hive_ce`/platform plugins; `presentation/` never imports any feature's `data/` directly; a BLoC/Cubit constructor never takes another BLoC/Cubit as a dependency.
39	- Structural seed to scaffold: `lib/core/{design_tokens.dart, network/, failure/, di/, cache/, resource.dart, isolated_side_effect.dart, session/}` and `lib/features/{auth, vault, entries, capture, chat, export, dashboard, account}/`, each pre-wired for `data/domain/presentation`.
40	- Full stack is pinned (Flutter 3.47.x via `fvm`; `flutter_bloc`, `go_router`, `dio`, `hive_ce`, `get_it`, `fpdart`, `freezed`, `json_serializable`, `mocktail`, `fl_chart`, `local_auth`, `flutter_secure_storage`, `flutter_dotenv`, `whisper_ggml` — exact versions in the architecture spine's stack-pins table) and must resolve with no conflicts before anything else is built.
41	- Design tokens (`colors`, `typography`, `rounded`, `spacing`, `components`, plus the two elevation constants) are implemented verbatim, camelCase, as the single source of truth; every other file reads from them, never redefines a value.
42	
43	## UX & Interaction Patterns
44	
45	- Single fixed frame: 390×844 logical points, portrait only, light mode only — no breakpoint, landscape, or dark-mode path anywhere in the app.
46	- Buttons and text fields come from one shared component set: disabled buttons always render `colorBorder` background + `colorTextSecondary` text (never dimmed opacity); text fields show distinct default/focused(`colorPrimary`, 1.5px)/error(`colorError`) border states.
47	- The side menu is the sole navigation hub (plus back arrows and sheet "x" closes) — no drawer-within-drawer, no tab bar. It must resolve all four destinations (chat session switching, Meus Registros, Configurações, Planos de Ação) without a 404 or crash.
48	- The Planos de Ação placeholder (an explicit, never-implemented extension feature) must still look fully finished — same visual polish as real screens, no graying-out, no backend calls, no drag/drop logic.
49	- The avatar component (solid `colorPrimary` circle, 1–2 uppercase initials, 40px) is built here for reuse, not reimplementation, when Configurações needs its 52px variant later (Epic 8).
50	- The "Sessão expirada" overlay is a scrim over the current screen using the confirmation-dialog component with a neutral (`colorTextPrimary`) title — never the red destructive-title variant. It traps focus until dismissed/actioned, is the only overlay allowed on screen at a time (never stacks on another open overlay), and its entrance uses only the `scrimIn` (0.18s) choreography — no other motion exists in the system besides `sheetUp` for bottom sheets.
51	- Copy for the overlay must avoid any language implying data loss or starting over; history and scroll position are understood by the user to be preserved.
52	
53	## Cross-Story Dependencies
54	
55	- Story 1.1 (DI, API client, Failure hierarchy, URL builder, retry interceptor, shared failure-matrix test helper) is a hard prerequisite for every other story in this epic and for every later epic's write-endpoint tests.
56	- Story 1.2's design tokens and base components (buttons, text fields, avatar) are consumed by Story 1.3's login/signup screen, Story 1.5's overlay, and Story 1.6's navigation shell/placeholders.
57	- Story 1.4 depends on Story 1.3's auth calls and exposes the singleton `SessionStatus` stream that Story 1.5 listens to and that the `go_router` redirect skeleton composes.
58	- Story 1.5's "Entrar novamente" action routes to the biometric/PIN re-auth flow that is not built until Epic 2 — this epic should wire the route target without implementing that flow.
59	- Story 1.6's `go_router` redirect skeleton is extended by Epic 2 (RF03), which plugs in the local vault-status gate ahead of the session gate already built here, in a fixed order (vault checked first).

- Single fixed frame: 390×844 logical points, portrait only, light mode only — no breakpoint, landscape, or dark-mode path anywhere in the app.

11:### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
12:Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).
18:### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
19:Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.
23:### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
30:### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
37:### RF05 — Personal summary export
44:### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
45:Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).

58:- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.

121:Minimalist identity, a warm and neutral palette, readable sans-serif typography, standardized components (buttons, chat bubbles, cards). This foundation is the direct object of RNF08. Tokens: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`.

input.prompt:
I'm planning Story 1.4 "Silent Session Refresh & Persistence" for a Flutter app (Clean Architecture, flutter_bloc, dio, get_it, flutter_secure_storage, fpdart Either<Failure,T>). I need a distilled investigation summary (file paths + line numbers, not full file dumps) covering:

1. `lib/core/network/access_token_provider.dart` — full current API surface (methods, what it persists, where it reads from secure storage). Does it currently save/read a refresh token at all, or only an access token?
2. `lib/core/network/api_client.dart` and `lib/core/network/header_interceptor.dart` (or wherever header logic lives) — how headers are currently attached (apikey vs Authorization bearer), and whether there's already a retry interceptor for `retryable:true` codes. Give exact line anchors.
3. `lib/core/failure/failure.dart` (or wherever the sealed Failure hierarchy lives) — list all ~14 subtypes verbatim, and note whether there's already something like `SessionExpired`/`Unauthorized`/`AuthInvalid`.
4. `lib/main.dart` — current full content (it's small). I need to know exactly how the app currently decides its home screen (I believe it's hardcoded to AuthScreen with a throwaway post-auth placeholder from story 1.3).
5. `lib/features/auth/` — current full file list and, for each of `domain/repositories/auth_repository.dart`, `data/repositories/auth_repository_impl.dart`, `data/datasources/auth_remote_data_source.dart`, `auth_injection.dart`: give me their current method signatures / DI registrations (not full bodies unless short).
6. `lib/core/session/` — confirm it's empty except `.gitkeep` (already known, just confirm no other files).
7. `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart` — how `registerAuthFeature()` and other core singletons are wired, exact line anchors, and whether there's a bootstrap order I need to respect.
8. Search the repo for any existing use of `go_router`, `SessionStatus`, or `Stream` anywhere outside node_modules/pub cache — confirm none exists yet (or report what you find).
9. In `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, find the full definitions for `POST /auth/refresh` and `GET /auth/session`: request/response schemas, which security scheme each uses (anon bearer vs user bearer vs none), and any notes on token expiry fields (e.g. `expiresAt`, `expiresIn`) in the login/signup/refresh response schema.
10. In `docs/input/backend/` (README and any error-taxonomy/known-bugs doc), find anything describing session-expiry behavior, the `x-cerne-function` name for refresh/session, retryable error codes, or known bugs related to auth/refresh/session.
11. Check `pubspec.yaml` for exact pinned versions of `dio`, `flutter_secure_storage`, `get_it`, `flutter_bloc`, `go_router`, `fpdart` — is `go_router` already a dependency even though unused?

Report back as a compact structured summary with file:line references for everything — I don't need prose explanations, just the facts I need to write a spec. Keep total response under ~700 lines, prioritize exact signatures/line numbers over narrative.

---
title: 'Story 1.4: Silent Session Refresh & Persistence'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-10-27'
status: 'draft'
review_loop_iteration: 0
baseline_commit: '8a4b94403d05281d58068aa4dac46dc08adf1873'
context:
  - '{project-root}/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-1-context.md'
  - '{project-root}/docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml'
  - '{project-root}/docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md'
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** `AccessTokenProvider` only persists the access token (`access_token_provider.dart:8-35`); the refresh token already decoded into `AuthResponseDto` is discarded (`auth_repository_impl.dart:63-65`), and `main.dart` hardcodes `AuthScreen` as home with zero bootstrap check (`main.dart:36-46`) — so a valid session never survives a restart.

**Approach:** Persist the refresh token; add a `SessionRepository` in the auth domain that, on launch, unconditionally exchanges any stored refresh token for a fresh pair via `auth-refresh`, exposing the result as the epic's one singleton `SessionStatus` stream. `main.dart` branches its `home` on that stream's first emission instead of hardcoding `AuthScreen`.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Boot calls `auth-refresh` once, unconditionally, whenever a refresh token is stored — no client-side expiry math or clock comparison; the server is the sole source of truth for validity.
- `AccessTokenProvider` gains `saveSession({accessToken, refreshToken})`, `readRefreshToken()`, `clearSession()`; existing `readAccessToken`/`saveAccessToken`/`clearAccessToken` stay untouched for `HeaderInterceptor` (`access_token_provider.dart:8-14`).
- `auth-refresh` stays in `HeaderInterceptor.anonKeyOnlyFunctions` (`header_interceptor.dart:20-24`) — refresh must never need the (possibly dead) access-token bearer.
- `SessionRepository.statusStream`/`restoreSession()` is the ONE new DI-singleton access point for session validity (epic AD) — no second stream, no raw-401 re-derivation.
- `AuthRepositoryImpl._authenticate` (`auth_repository_impl.dart:46-74`) persists the refresh token returned by signup/login too, via the same `saveSession`.
- A dead/missing refresh token reuses the closed 14-subtype `Failure` hierarchy (`AuthExpired`/`AuthInvalid`) — no new subtype (`failure.dart`).

**Ask First:** if the backend's `auth-refresh` response omits any field `openapi.yaml:197-234` marks required, HALT before guessing a fallback.

**Never:**
- No reactive refresh-and-retry-on-401 interceptor — mid-session expiry while the app is running is Story 1.5's overlay scope, not this story's.
- No `go_router` wiring (Story 1.6) — `main.dart` keeps its current `MaterialApp`/`Navigator` shape; only `home` changes.
- No new Cubit for this story — `main.dart` drives directly off `SessionRepository`.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Cold boot, valid refresh token | refreshToken stored, backend accepts | `auth-refresh` succeeds, new pair saved, stream emits `authenticated`, home = post-auth placeholder | N/A |
| Cold boot, no stored session | no refresh token (fresh install / post-logout) | no network call, stream emits `unauthenticated` immediately, home = `AuthScreen` | N/A |
| Cold boot, dead refresh token | refreshToken stored, backend returns `AUTH_EXPIRED`/`AUTH_INVALID` | session cleared, stream emits `unauthenticated`, home = `AuthScreen` | silent — no error UI |
| Cold boot, offline | refreshToken stored, no connectivity | stream emits `unauthenticated` (fail-closed), storage left untouched | silent; next boot retries naturally |
| Successful signup/login (1.3 path) | — | refresh token now also saved via `saveSession` | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/core/network/access_token_provider.dart:8-35` -- add `saveSession`/`readRefreshToken`/`clearSession` to the abstract port + the `FlutterSecureStorage` impl (new key alongside existing `_key`).
- `lib/features/auth/data/models/auth_response_dto.dart` -- `AuthSessionDto` already decodes `refreshToken`; reuse as-is, no DTO change.
- `lib/features/auth/data/datasources/auth_remote_data_source.dart:12-47` -- add `refresh(String refreshToken)`, posting `{refreshToken}` to `auth-refresh` (own body shape, can't reuse the email/password `_post` helper as-is).
- `lib/features/auth/data/repositories/auth_repository_impl.dart:46-74` -- `_authenticate` calls `saveSession(...)` instead of `saveAccessToken` only.
- `lib/features/auth/domain/entities/session_status.dart` -- new: `enum SessionStatus { authenticated, unauthenticated }`.
- `lib/features/auth/domain/repositories/session_repository.dart` -- new: `Stream<SessionStatus> get statusStream; Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> restoreSession();`.
- `lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart` -- new: owns the broadcast `StreamController`, calls `AuthRemoteDataSource.refresh`, persists/clears via `AccessTokenProvider`.
- `lib/features/auth/auth_injection.dart:13-24` -- register `SessionRepository` singleton (after `AccessTokenProvider`/`AuthRemoteDataSource`).
- `lib/main.dart:23-67` -- `CerneApp` calls `sl<SessionRepository>().restoreSession()` once, branches `home` on a `StreamBuilder<SessionStatus>` (no-data yet = brief blank, per RNF01's 300ms threshold) between `AuthScreen` and the existing `_PostAuthPlaceholder`.
- `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:179-240` -- `auth-refresh` ground truth: `{refreshToken}` in, same `session` shape out, `security: []`.

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] `access_token_provider.dart` -- add `saveSession`/`readRefreshToken`/`clearSession` -- new secure-storage surface for the refresh token
- [ ] `auth_remote_data_source.dart` -- add `refresh()` -- calls `auth-refresh` per contract
- [ ] `auth_repository_impl.dart` -- `_authenticate` persists the refresh token too -- closes the gap 1.3 flagged
- [ ] `session_status.dart` -- new enum -- the two-state status the epic's AD requires
- [ ] `session_repository.dart` (domain) + `session_repository_impl.dart` (data) -- new -- singleton stream + boot-time restore
- [ ] `auth_injection.dart` -- register `SessionRepository` -- DI wiring
- [ ] `main.dart` -- boot-time `restoreSession()` + `StreamBuilder` home branch -- replaces the hardcoded `AuthScreen` home
- [ ] `test/.../session_repository_impl_test.dart` -- cover the I/O matrix rows (valid/none/dead/offline) with `mocktail`
- [ ] `test/.../auth_remote_data_source_test.dart` -- `refresh()` write-failure matrix (timeout/malformed/offline) per RNF09
- [ ] `test/main_test.dart` -- extend for both boot branches (authenticated vs unauthenticated home)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given a stored refresh token the backend accepts, when the app launches, then the user reaches the authenticated placeholder with no login prompt and no visible loading UI in the happy path (<300ms).
- Given no stored session or a refresh token the backend rejects, when the app launches, then the user lands on `AuthScreen` with no error message shown.
- Given a successful signup/login, when `AuthRepositoryImpl` returns, then both the access token and refresh token are persisted, unchanged `Either<Failure,T>` signature (RNF09).

## Design Notes

- `StreamBuilder` over a Cubit: `SessionRepository` already exposes a `Stream`; wrapping it in a Cubit just to re-expose the same stream would be a redundant layer — Story 1.6's nav shell/`go_router` redirect consumes it directly instead.
- Unconditional refresh-at-boot (no client-side expiry math) trades one always-on network round trip for zero clock-skew bugs; revisit only if the 300ms-threshold UX proves this too slow in practice.
- Mid-session reactive refresh-on-401 is deliberately deferred to Story 1.5 (the overlay) rather than solved here with a second mechanism.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter pub get` -- resolves, no conflicts
- `fvm flutter test` -- all tests pass
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- zero issues
- `grep -rn "Color(0x\|fontSize:\|EdgeInsets\.\(all\|symmetric\|only\)(" lib/features/auth lib/core/network --include=*.dart` -- expected: no matches (RNF08)

2	title: 'Story 1.4: Silent Session Refresh & Persistence'
3	type: 'feature'
4	created: '2026-10-27'
5	status: 'review'
6	review_loop_iteration: 0
7	baseline_commit: '8a4b94403d05281d58068aa4dac46dc08adf1873'

13	
14	<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">
15	
16	## Intent
17	
18	**Problem:** `AccessTokenProvider` only persists the access token (`access_token_provider.dart:8-35`); the refresh token already decoded into `AuthResponseDto` is discarded (`auth_repository_impl.dart:63-65`), and `main.dart` hardcodes `AuthScreen` as home with zero bootstrap check (`main.dart:36-46`) — so a valid session never survives a restart.
19	
20	**Approach:** Persist the refresh token; add a `SessionRepository` in the auth domain that, on launch, unconditionally exchanges any stored refresh token for a fresh pair via `auth-refresh`, exposing the result as the epic's one singleton `SessionStatus` stream. `main.dart` branches its `home` on that stream's first emission instead of hardcoding `AuthScreen`.
21	
22	## Boundaries & Constraints
23	
24	**Always:**
25	- Boot calls `auth-refresh` once, unconditionally, whenever a refresh token is stored — no client-side expiry math or clock comparison; the server is the sole source of truth for validity.
26	- `AccessTokenProvider` gains `saveSession({accessToken, refreshToken})`, `readRefreshToken()`, `clearSession()`; existing `readAccessToken`/`saveAccessToken`/`clearAccessToken` stay untouched for `HeaderInterceptor` (`access_token_provider.dart:8-14`).
27	- `auth-refresh` stays in `HeaderInterceptor.anonKeyOnlyFunctions` (`header_interceptor.dart:20-24`) — refresh must never need the (possibly dead) access-token bearer.
28	- `SessionRepository.statusStream`/`restoreSession()` is the ONE new DI-singleton access point for session validity (epic AD) — no second stream, no raw-401 re-derivation.
29	- `AuthRepositoryImpl._authenticate` (`auth_repository_impl.dart:46-74`) persists the refresh token returned by signup/login too, via the same `saveSession`.
30	- A dead/missing refresh token reuses the closed 14-subtype `Failure` hierarchy (`AuthExpired`/`AuthInvalid`) — no new subtype (`failure.dart`).
31	
32	**Ask First:** if the backend's `auth-refresh` response omits any field `openapi.yaml:197-234` marks required, HALT before guessing a fallback.
33	
34	**Never:**
35	- No reactive refresh-and-retry-on-401 interceptor — mid-session expiry while the app is running is Story 1.5's overlay scope, not this story's.
36	- No `go_router` wiring (Story 1.6) — `main.dart` keeps its current `MaterialApp`/`Navigator` shape; only `home` changes.
37	- No new Cubit for this story — `main.dart` drives directly off `SessionRepository`.
38	
39	## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
40	
41	| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
42	|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
43	| Cold boot, valid refresh token | refreshToken stored, backend accepts | `auth-refresh` succeeds, new pair saved, stream emits `authenticated`, home = post-auth placeholder | N/A |
44	| Cold boot, no stored session | no refresh token (fresh install / post-logout) | no network call, stream emits `unauthenticated` immediately, home = `AuthScreen` | N/A |
45	| Cold boot, dead refresh token | refreshToken stored, backend returns `AUTH_EXPIRED`/`AUTH_INVALID` | session cleared, stream emits `unauthenticated`, home = `AuthScreen` | silent — no error UI |
46	| Cold boot, offline | refreshToken stored, no connectivity | stream emits `unauthenticated` (fail-closed), storage left untouched | silent; next boot retries naturally |
47	| Successful signup/login (1.3 path) | — | refresh token now also saved via `saveSession` | N/A |
48	
49	</frozen-after-approval>
50	
51	## Code Map
52

---
title: 'Story 1.4: Silent Session Refresh & Persistence'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-10-27'
status: 'review'
review_loop_iteration: 0
baseline_commit: '8a4b94403d05281d58068aa4dac46dc08adf1873'
context:
  - '{project-root}/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-1-context.md'
  - '{project-root}/docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml'
  - '{project-root}/docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md'
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** `AccessTokenProvider` only persists the access token (`access_token_provider.dart:8-35`); the refresh token already decoded into `AuthResponseDto` is discarded (`auth_repository_impl.dart:63-65`), and `main.dart` hardcodes `AuthScreen` as home with zero bootstrap check (`main.dart:36-46`) — so a valid session never survives a restart.

**Approach:** Persist the refresh token; add a `SessionRepository` in the auth domain that, on launch, unconditionally exchanges any stored refresh token for a fresh pair via `auth-refresh`, exposing the result as the epic's one singleton `SessionStatus` stream. `main.dart` branches its `home` on that stream's first emission instead of hardcoding `AuthScreen`.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Boot calls `auth-refresh` once, unconditionally, whenever a refresh token is stored — no client-side expiry math or clock comparison; the server is the sole source of truth for validity.
- `AccessTokenProvider` gains `saveSession({accessToken, refreshToken})`, `readRefreshToken()`, `clearSession()`; existing `readAccessToken`/`saveAccessToken`/`clearAccessToken` stay untouched for `HeaderInterceptor` (`access_token_provider.dart:8-14`).
- `auth-refresh` stays in `HeaderInterceptor.anonKeyOnlyFunctions` (`header_interceptor.dart:20-24`) — refresh must never need the (possibly dead) access-token bearer.
- `SessionRepository.statusStream`/`restoreSession()` is the ONE new DI-singleton access point for session validity (epic AD) — no second stream, no raw-401 re-derivation.
- `AuthRepositoryImpl._authenticate` (`auth_repository_impl.dart:46-74`) persists the refresh token returned by signup/login too, via the same `saveSession`.
- A dead/missing refresh token reuses the closed 14-subtype `Failure` hierarchy (`AuthExpired`/`AuthInvalid`) — no new subtype (`failure.dart`).

**Ask First:** if the backend's `auth-refresh` response omits any field `openapi.yaml:197-234` marks required, HALT before guessing a fallback.

**Never:**
- No reactive refresh-and-retry-on-401 interceptor — mid-session expiry while the app is running is Story 1.5's overlay scope, not this story's.
- No `go_router` wiring (Story 1.6) — `main.dart` keeps its current `MaterialApp`/`Navigator` shape; only `home` changes.
- No new Cubit for this story — `main.dart` drives directly off `SessionRepository`.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Cold boot, valid refresh token | refreshToken stored, backend accepts | `auth-refresh` succeeds, new pair saved, stream emits `authenticated`, home = post-auth placeholder | N/A |
| Cold boot, no stored session | no refresh token (fresh install / post-logout) | no network call, stream emits `unauthenticated` immediately, home = `AuthScreen` | N/A |
| Cold boot, dead refresh token | refreshToken stored, backend returns `AUTH_EXPIRED`/`AUTH_INVALID` | session cleared, stream emits `unauthenticated`, home = `AuthScreen` | silent — no error UI |
| Cold boot, offline | refreshToken stored, no connectivity | stream emits `unauthenticated` (fail-closed), storage left untouched | silent; next boot retries naturally |
| Successful signup/login (1.3 path) | — | refresh token now also saved via `saveSession` | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/core/network/access_token_provider.dart:8-35` -- add `saveSession`/`readRefreshToken`/`clearSession` to the abstract port + the `FlutterSecureStorage` impl (new key alongside existing `_key`).
- `lib/features/auth/data/models/auth_response_dto.dart` -- `AuthSessionDto` already decodes `refreshToken`; reuse as-is, no DTO change.
- `lib/features/auth/data/datasources/auth_remote_data_source.dart:12-47` -- add `refresh(String refreshToken)`, posting `{refreshToken}` to `auth-refresh` (own body shape, can't reuse the email/password `_post` helper as-is).
- `lib/features/auth/data/repositories/auth_repository_impl.dart:46-74` -- `_authenticate` calls `saveSession(...)` instead of `saveAccessToken` only.
- `lib/features/auth/domain/entities/session_status.dart` -- new: `enum SessionStatus { authenticated, unauthenticated }`.
- `lib/features/auth/domain/repositories/session_repository.dart` -- new: `Stream<SessionStatus> get statusStream; Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> restoreSession();`.
- `lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart` -- new: owns the broadcast `StreamController`, calls `AuthRemoteDataSource.refresh`, persists/clears via `AccessTokenProvider`.
- `lib/features/auth/auth_injection.dart:13-24` -- register `SessionRepository` singleton (after `AccessTokenProvider`/`AuthRemoteDataSource`).
- `lib/main.dart:23-67` -- `CerneApp` calls `sl<SessionRepository>().restoreSession()` once, branches `home` on a `StreamBuilder<SessionStatus>` (no-data yet = brief blank, per RNF01's 300ms threshold) between `AuthScreen` and the existing `_PostAuthPlaceholder`.
- `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:179-240` -- `auth-refresh` ground truth: `{refreshToken}` in, same `session` shape out, `security: []`.

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [x] `access_token_provider.dart` -- add `saveSession`/`readRefreshToken`/`clearSession` -- new secure-storage surface for the refresh token
- [x] `auth_remote_data_source.dart` -- add `refresh()` -- calls `auth-refresh` per contract
- [x] `auth_repository_impl.dart` -- `_authenticate` persists the refresh token too -- closes the gap 1.3 flagged
- [x] `session_status.dart` -- new enum -- the two-state status the epic's AD requires
- [x] `session_repository.dart` (domain) + `session_repository_impl.dart` (data) -- new -- singleton stream + boot-time restore
- [x] `auth_injection.dart` -- register `SessionRepository` -- DI wiring
- [x] `main.dart` -- boot-time `restoreSession()` + `StreamBuilder` home branch -- replaces the hardcoded `AuthScreen` home
- [x] `test/.../session_repository_impl_test.dart` -- cover the I/O matrix rows (valid/none/dead/offline) with `mocktail`
- [x] `test/.../auth_remote_data_source_test.dart` -- `refresh()` write-failure matrix (timeout/malformed/offline) per RNF09
- [x] `test/main_test.dart` -- extend for both boot branches (authenticated vs unauthenticated home)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given a stored refresh token the backend accepts, when the app launches, then the user reaches the authenticated placeholder with no login prompt and no visible loading UI in the happy path (<300ms).
- Given no stored session or a refresh token the backend rejects, when the app launches, then the user lands on `AuthScreen` with no error message shown.
- Given a successful signup/login, when `AuthRepositoryImpl` returns, then both the access token and refresh token are persisted, unchanged `Either<Failure,T>` signature (RNF09).

## Design Notes

- `StreamBuilder` over a Cubit: `SessionRepository` already exposes a `Stream`; wrapping it in a Cubit just to re-expose the same stream would be a redundant layer — Story 1.6's nav shell/`go_router` redirect consumes it directly instead.
- Unconditional refresh-at-boot (no client-side expiry math) trades one always-on network round trip for zero clock-skew bugs; revisit only if the 300ms-threshold UX proves this too slow in practice.
- Mid-session reactive refresh-on-401 is deliberately deferred to Story 1.5 (the overlay) rather than solved here with a second mechanism.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter pub get` -- resolves, no conflicts
- `fvm flutter test` -- all tests pass
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- zero issues
- `grep -rn "Color(0x\|fontSize:\|EdgeInsets\.\(all\|symmetric\|only\)(" lib/features/auth lib/core/network --include=*.dart` -- expected: no matches (RNF08)

title: 'Story 1.4: Silent Session Refresh & Persistence'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-10-27'
status: 'review'
review_loop_iteration: 0
baseline_commit: '8a4b94403d05281d58068aa4dac46dc08adf1873'
context:

  - '{project-root}/docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml'
  - '{project-root}/docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md'
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** `AccessTokenProvider` only persists the access token (`access_token_provider.dart:8-35`); the refresh token already decoded into `AuthResponseDto` is discarded (`auth_repository_impl.dart:63-65`), and `main.dart` hardcodes `AuthScreen` as home with zero bootstrap check (`main.dart:36-46`) — so a valid session never survives a restart.

**Approach:** Persist the refresh token; add a `SessionRepository` in the auth domain that, on launch, unconditionally exchanges any stored refresh token for a fresh pair via `auth-refresh`, exposing the result as the epic's one singleton `SessionStatus` stream. `main.dart` branches its `home` on that stream's first emission instead of hardcoding `AuthScreen`.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Boot calls `auth-refresh` once, unconditionally, whenever a refresh token is stored — no client-side expiry math or clock comparison; the server is the sole source of truth for validity.
- `AccessTokenProvider` gains `saveSession({accessToken, refreshToken})`, `readRefreshToken()`, `clearSession()`; existing `readAccessToken`/`saveAccessToken`/`clearAccessToken` stay untouched for `HeaderInterceptor` (`access_token_provider.dart:8-14`).
- `auth-refresh` stays in `HeaderInterceptor.anonKeyOnlyFunctions` (`header_interceptor.dart:20-24`) — refresh must never need the (possibly dead) access-token bearer.
- `SessionRepository.statusStream`/`restoreSession()` is the ONE new DI-singleton access point for session validity (epic AD) — no second stream, no raw-401 re-derivation.
- `AuthRepositoryImpl._authenticate` (`auth_repository_impl.dart:46-74`) persists the refresh token returned by signup/login too, via the same `saveSession`.
- A dead/missing refresh token reuses the closed 14-subtype `Failure` hierarchy (`AuthExpired`/`AuthInvalid`) — no new subtype (`failure.dart`).

**Ask First:** if the backend's `auth-refresh` response omits any field `openapi.yaml:197-234` marks required, HALT before guessing a fallback.

**Never:**
- No reactive refresh-and-retry-on-401 interceptor — mid-session expiry while the app is running is Story 1.5's overlay scope, not this story's.
- No `go_router` wiring (Story 1.6) — `main.dart` keeps its current `MaterialApp`/`Navigator` shape; only `home` changes.
- No new Cubit for this story — `main.dart` drives directly off `SessionRepository`.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Cold boot, valid refresh token | refreshToken stored, backend accepts | `auth-refresh` succeeds, new pair saved, stream emits `authenticated`, home = post-auth placeholder | N/A |
| Cold boot, no stored session | no refresh token (fresh install / post-logout) | no network call, stream emits `unauthenticated` immediately, home = `AuthScreen` | N/A |
| Cold boot, dead refresh token | refreshToken stored, backend returns `AUTH_EXPIRED`/`AUTH_INVALID` | session cleared, stream emits `unauthenticated`, home = `AuthScreen` | silent — no error UI |
| Cold boot, offline | refreshToken stored, no connectivity | stream emits `unauthenticated` (fail-closed), storage left untouched | silent; next boot retries naturally |
| Successful signup/login (1.3 path) | — | refresh token now also saved via `saveSession` | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/core/network/access_token_provider.dart:8-35` -- add `saveSession`/`readRefreshToken`/`clearSession` to the abstract port + the `FlutterSecureStorage` impl (new key alongside existing `_key`).
- `lib/features/auth/data/models/auth_response_dto.dart` -- `AuthSessionDto` already decodes `refreshToken`; reuse as-is, no DTO change.
- `lib/features/auth/data/datasources/auth_remote_data_source.dart:12-47` -- add `refresh(String refreshToken)`, posting `{refreshToken}` to `auth-refresh` (own body shape, can't reuse the email/password `_post` helper as-is).
- `lib/features/auth/data/repositories/auth_repository_impl.dart:46-74` -- `_authenticate` calls `saveSession(...)` instead of `saveAccessToken` only.
- `lib/features/auth/domain/entities/session_status.dart` -- new: `enum SessionStatus { authenticated, unauthenticated }`.
- `lib/features/auth/domain/repositories/session_repository.dart` -- new: `Stream<SessionStatus> get statusStream; Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> restoreSession();`.
- `lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart` -- new: owns the broadcast `StreamController`, calls `AuthRemoteDataSource.refresh`, persists/clears via `AccessTokenProvider`.
- `lib/features/auth/auth_injection.dart:13-24` -- register `SessionRepository` singleton (after `AccessTokenProvider`/`AuthRemoteDataSource`).
- `lib/main.dart:23-67` -- `CerneApp` calls `sl<SessionRepository>().restoreSession()` once, branches `home` on a `StreamBuilder<SessionStatus>` (no-data yet = brief blank, per RNF01's 300ms threshold) between `AuthScreen` and the existing `_PostAuthPlaceholder`.
- `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:179-240` -- `auth-refresh` ground truth: `{refreshToken}` in, same `session` shape out, `security: []`.

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [x] `access_token_provider.dart` -- add `saveSession`/`readRefreshToken`/`clearSession` -- new secure-storage surface for the refresh token
- [x] `auth_remote_data_source.dart` -- add `refresh()` -- calls `auth-refresh` per contract
- [x] `auth_repository_impl.dart` -- `_authenticate` persists the refresh token too -- closes the gap 1.3 flagged
- [x] `session_status.dart` -- new enum -- the two-state status the epic's AD requires
- [x] `session_repository.dart` (domain) + `session_repository_impl.dart` (data) -- new -- singleton stream + boot-time restore
- [x] `auth_injection.dart` -- register `SessionRepository` -- DI wiring
- [x] `main.dart` -- boot-time `restoreSession()` + `StreamBuilder` home branch -- replaces the hardcoded `AuthScreen` home
- [x] `test/.../session_repository_impl_test.dart` -- cover the I/O matrix rows (valid/none/dead/offline) with `mocktail`
- [x] `test/.../auth_remote_data_source_test.dart` -- `refresh()` write-failure matrix (timeout/malformed/offline) per RNF09
- [x] `test/main_test.dart` -- extend for both boot branches (authenticated vs unauthenticated home)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given a stored refresh token the backend accepts, when the app launches, then the user reaches the authenticated placeholder with no login prompt and no visible loading UI in the happy path (<300ms).
- Given no stored session or a refresh token the backend rejects, when the app launches, then the user lands on `AuthScreen` with no error message shown.
- Given a successful signup/login, when `AuthRepositoryImpl` returns, then both the access token and refresh token are persisted, unchanged `Either<Failure,T>` signature (RNF09).

## Design Notes

- `StreamBuilder` over a Cubit: `SessionRepository` already exposes a `Stream`; wrapping it in a Cubit just to re-expose the same stream would be a redundant layer — Story 1.6's nav shell/`go_router` redirect consumes it directly instead.
- Unconditional refresh-at-boot (no client-side expiry math) trades one always-on network round trip for zero clock-skew bugs; revisit only if the 300ms-threshold UX proves this too slow in practice.
- Mid-session reactive refresh-on-401 is deliberately deferred to Story 1.5 (the overlay) rather than solved here with a second mechanism.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter pub get` -- resolves, no conflicts
- `fvm flutter test` -- all tests pass
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- zero issues
- `grep -rn "Color(0x\|fontSize:\|EdgeInsets\.\(all\|symmetric\|only\)(" lib/features/auth lib/core/network --include=*.dart` -- expected: no matches (RNF08)

+# Story 1.2 — Design Token System & Core Component Library
+
+## Context
+
+Story 1.2 delivered `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` and three shared widgets
+(`AppButton`, `AppTextField`, `Avatar`). Each component already had thorough
+*isolated* widget tests (one component at a time, checked against
+`DesignTokens` values). The gap: nothing proved the shared text-field/button
+primitives work together the way a consuming screen composes them — user
+keystrokes, taps, and focus changes flowing through multiple widgets in the
+same tree. That is a gap in the component library's own test coverage, not a
+screen's — it holds regardless of which feature consumes the widgets, and
+still no device/simulator/CI pipeline exists (AGENTS.md), so a traditional
+on-device E2E run isn't possible either way.
+
+(Story 1.3's actual login screen, `auth_screen.dart`, already shipped by the
+time of this round of patches — see `git log`. Its own `auth_screen_test.dart`
+is BLoC/cubit-focused and doesn't exercise raw widget interaction such as
+obscured-text-while-typing, keyboard-action focus movement, or a disabled
+button's `onPressed` actually staying `null`; this harness is not a stand-in
+for that screen, it covers what that screen's test suite does not.)
+
+## Generated Tests
+
+### Composition/interaction tests (shared widget library, user-driven)
+
+- [x] `test/core/widgets/component_library_interaction_test.dart` — a
+      `StatefulWidget` test harness (test-only, not shipped code) composing
+      two `AppTextField`s + one `AppButton` the way a form screen will.
+      Covers, through real taps and keystrokes:
+  - submit button stays disabled (`onPressed: null`) until both fields are
+    non-empty, and enables once they are.
+  - tapping the enabled button delivers the typed e-mail and senha values.
+  - an invalid e-mail surfaces the error border (`colorError`, 1.5px
+    `borderWidthEmphasis`) and error text, and never calls the submit
+    callback.
+  - correcting the e-mail after an invalid submit and resubmitting clears
+    the error and calls the submit callback.
+  - pressing the keyboard's "next" action on the e-mail field moves focus
+    to the senha field (`TextField`'s built-in default behavior — no extra
+    wiring needed).
+  - the senha field stays obscured while typing.
+  - a disabled button's `onPressed` is actually `null`, and tapping it never
+    fires the callback.
+  - the whole composed form renders with no overflow/exception at a 3.0x
+    Dynamic Type scale.
+
+No new API endpoints exist for this story (pure UI/design-system work).
+
+## Coverage
+
+- Core component library: unit-level coverage already complete
+  (pre-existing, one widget at a time); this pass adds the missing
+  cross-component interaction coverage.
+- UI features: Story 1.3's login/signup screen is covered by its own
+  `auth_screen_test.dart` (BLoC-focused); this harness covers the shared
+  widgets' interaction behavior independent of any one screen.
+
+## Verification
+
+- `fvm flutter test` — 169/169 passing (161 pre-existing + 8 new).
+- `fvm flutter analyze` — no issues found.
+
+## Next Steps
+
+- Revisit true device E2E once a device/simulator or CI step exists
+  (AGENTS.md's open TODO).

+# Story 1.3 — Account Creation and Login
+
+## Context
+
+Story 1.3 delivered the first real feature screen (`AuthScreen`, Tela 0.1a)
+and the first feature-level API surface (`auth-login`/`auth-signup`). Unlike
+stories 1.1 and 1.2, the dev-story and code-review passes for this story
+already produced both an E2E-shaped screen test and an API-shaped repository
+test directly — this pass's job is to audit that coverage against the
+story's own I/O matrix (`spec-1-3-account-creation-and-login.md`) rather than
+author it from scratch, and to record the audit here since this file hadn't
+been updated since story 1.2.
+
+No device/simulator/CI pipeline exists yet (AGENTS.md), so "E2E" here still
+means the same thing it meant for stories 1.1/1.2: drive the real composition
+through `flutter_test`, faking only the one boundary each layer can't avoid
+(the native secure-storage channel, or the HTTP transport) — not a
+traditional on-device run.
+
+## Audited Tests (pre-existing, not newly generated this pass)
+
+### E2E (screen- and composition-root-level, user-driven)
+
+- [x] `test/features/auth/presentation/screens/auth_screen_test.dart` — real
+      `AuthCubit` + mocked `AuthRepository`, driven via actual taps/keystrokes
+      on `AuthScreen`. Covers every row of the story's I/O matrix: valid
+      login, valid signup (exactly `{email, password}`), `AUTH_INVALID` in
+      both login and signup mode (both fields bordered, message shown once,
+      typed values kept), malformed e-mail blocked pre-network, empty
+      password blocked pre-network, a generic network failure rendered via
+      `Failure.message`, and no overflow at 3.0x Dynamic Type.
+- [x] `test/main_test.dart` — the one test that exercises the real
+      composition root (`CerneApp` → `sl<AuthCubit>()` → `onAuthenticated` →
+      `Navigator.pushReplacement`), added as a code-review patch for this
+      story (`spec-1-3-account-creation-and-login.md`, Review Findings). Only
+      `AuthRepository` is swapped for a mock; DI, the real cubit, and the
+      real navigation callback all run unchanged.
+
+### API (repository/data-source level, real wiring down to the HTTP boundary)
+
+- [x] `test/features/auth/data/repositories/auth_repository_impl_test.dart`
+      — real `AuthRemoteDataSource` (so the real DTO `fromJson`/request-body
+      shape is exercised), only `ApiClient` mocked. Runs the project's
+      standard `runWriteFailureMatrix` across `auth-signup` and `auth-login`
+      (3 failure types each) plus success mapping and the
+      save-token-before-`Right` ordering.
+- [x] `test/core/network/network_pipeline_integration_test.dart` (story 1.1)
+      already uses `auth-login` as its anon-only-operation example end to
+      end through the real `Dio` + both real interceptors + `UrlBuilder`,
+      with only the `HttpClientAdapter` faked — so the feature's actual
+      operation name is proven to reach the wire correctly, not just a
+      generic placeholder.
+
+## Gap Analysis — no new tests generated
+
+Between the two layers above, every AC and I/O-matrix row already has
+coverage, and the split mirrors this codebase's established pattern (each
+integration test fakes exactly one boundary, per `bootstrap_integration_test.dart`'s
+and `network_pipeline_integration_test.dart`'s own stated scope). A third
+test re-driving `auth-login`/`auth-signup` through the full stack with only
+transport faked would duplicate assertions already made in the two tests
+above without proving anything new, so none was added (skill guidance:
+avoid unnecessary abstractions/duplication).
+
+## Coverage
+
+- Auth feature: validators, cubit, repository/data-source, screen, and
+  composition root are each covered at the layer where coverage is cheapest
+  and clearest — no layer is untested.
+- API endpoints introduced by this story: `auth-login`, `auth-signup` — both
+  covered at the repository layer (full failure matrix) and proven to reach
+  the real wire at the pipeline layer.
+
+## Verification

+- `fvm flutter analyze` — no issues found.

+## Next Steps

  Review of CONTENT (story 1.4 — Silent Session Refresh & Persistence — diff + new-file dumps). Findings:
  
  - `SessionRepositoryImpl.statusStream` is a plain `StreamController<SessionStatus>.broadcast()` with no replay/last-value cache and no `close()`/dispose hook (`lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart`). It is registered as a `registerLazySingleton`, and `resetCoreDependencies()` (`sl.reset()` in `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart`) does not call `close()` on it since nothing implements a disposing hook — the controller leaks every time DI is reset (every test in `test/main_test.dart` and `test/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl_test.dart`).
  
  - `main.dart`'s correctness depends on an unstated ordering guarantee: `_CerneAppState.initState()` fires `unawaited(_sessionRepository.restoreSession())`, and the very next `build()` subscribes a `StreamBuilder` to the same (non-replaying) broadcast stream. This only works because Flutter runs `initState → build` synchronously before any microtask from `restoreSession()`'s first `await` can execute. Nothing documents or guards this assumption (no cached "last known status" fallback) — a future refactor that inserts any `await` before the `StreamBuilder` is built (or moves the call earlier) would silently drop the one-and-only status emission and leave the UI stuck on the blank boot `Scaffold` forever.
  
  - After a successful login/signup, `SessionRepository.statusStream` is never updated to `authenticated` — `AuthCubit.submit()`/`AuthRepositoryImpl` persist tokens but don't touch `SessionRepository`, and the post-auth transition in `lib/main.dart` happens purely via `Navigator.pushReplacement`, bypassing the "ONE new DI-singleton access point for session validity" the story's own AD/Code Map mandates. If `CerneApp`'s `home` is ever rebuilt from scratch before an app restart (not just this story's happy path), the `StreamBuilder` would still report `unauthenticated` and show `AuthScreen` again despite a live session. No test exercises "login succeeds → statusStream reflects authenticated."
  
  - The I/O-Edge-Case Matrix in `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-1-4-silent-session-refresh-persistence.md` has no row for "refresh exchange succeeds but the local `saveSession` write throws." The code handles it (`session_repository_impl.dart`'s success branch catches and emits `unauthenticated`/`malformedResponse`), but since GoTrue-style refresh tokens are typically single-use/rotating, a persistence failure right after a successful exchange can strand the user (old refresh token already invalidated server-side, new one never saved) with no retry — an untested, undocumented edge case.
  
  - `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-1-4-silent-session-refresh-persistence.md` frontmatter declares `status: 'in-review'`, but `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/sprint-status.yaml` records `1-4-silent-session-refresh-persistence: in-progress` — the two tracking artifacts disagree on the story's actual state.
  
  - `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/tests/test-summary.md` gets no "Story 1.4" section at all in this diff, despite three new/extended test files landing (`session_repository_impl_test.dart`, `auth_remote_data_source_test.dart`, extended `main_test.dart`). This directly breaks a promise the same file already made for itself: Story 1.3's section explicitly says "When story 1.4 (silent session refresh) lands, extend `network_pipeline_integration_test.dart`-style real-wiring coverage to the refresh-token operation, and add the equivalent repository-layer failure matrix for it" — neither half happened (see next finding), and there's no updated test count/verification entry for 1.4 at all.
  
  - No real-wire pipeline test proves `auth-refresh` actually goes out with the anon key (not a stale/absent access-token bearer), the way `test/core/network/network_pipeline_integration_test.dart` explicitly proves for `auth-login`. `HeaderInterceptor.anonKeyOnlyFunctions` does already list `auth-refresh` (pre-existing, confirmed in `lib/core/network/header_interceptor.dart:20-24`), but this story adds the first real caller of that operation and never adds the equivalent pipeline-level assertion for it — a regression there would only be caught by the data-source-level test, which mocks `ApiClient` and can't observe headers.
  
  - In `test/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl_test.dart`, the "cold boot, no stored session" test only asserts `result!.isLeft()` is `true`, unlike the sibling "dead refresh token" tests which assert `isA<AuthExpired>()`/`isA<AuthInvalid>()` specifically. A change that silently swapped the returned failure type for the no-session branch would pass this test undetected.

Any later logging/analytics/UX branching keyed on failure type (crash-free-session metrics, etc.) won't be able to tell a brand-new install apart from an actual expiry.

2	  summary: No portrait-only orientation lock is enforced anywhere in the app shell (`ios/Runner/Info.plist` still lists landscape orientations alongside portrait).
3	  evidence: `docs/input/requirements.md` fixes the app to a single 390x844 portrait-only frame with no landscape path, but Story 1.1 is core infrastructure only (no screens/app-shell UI) and the architecture spine doesn't assign this lock to any specific story. Likely belongs to Story 1.6 (Base Navigation Shell with Feature Placeholders), the first story that builds real app-shell UI — should be picked up there rather than silently falling through the cracks.
4	
5	- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-1-2-design-token-system-core-component-library.md`
6	  summary: `lib/core/widgets/avatar.dart`'s `Avatar` renders raw initials text with no `Semantics` wrapper, so a screen reader announces e.g. "W D" instead of something like "Avatar, Wagner Duarte".
7	  evidence: Accessibility semantics were never required by Story 1.2's spec (no boundary, acceptance criterion, or epic-context requirement mentions it) and the prototype gives no guidance either, so adding it now would be scope creep beyond the frozen intent. Worth a deliberate pass across all shared widgets (button/text-field/avatar) once an accessibility requirement exists, rather than bolting it onto one widget ad hoc.

10	
11	- `AppButton` has no loading/busy state, even though most of its real call sites (login submit, insertion-modal "Salvar", export actions) are async network calls. Not required by Story 1.2's boundaries (§6's button component table lists only normal/pressed/disabled variations) — pick up when the first async-submit screen (Story 1.3) needs it, rather than letting each feature improvise its own busy treatment.
12	- `AppTextField` exposes no `enabled`/`readOnly`, `onSubmitted`, `autofocus`, `textCapitalization`, or `inputFormatters` — all plausible needs for the upcoming login/signup and inline-name-edit screens. Not required by Story 1.2's acceptance criteria; let Story 1.3 (its first real consumer) request exactly what it needs instead of speculatively widening the shared primitive now.
13	- `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` now imports `package:flutter/widgets.dart` (needed for `Color`/`TextStyle`/`EdgeInsets`/`BoxShadow`), but nothing in the repo (lint rule or architecture test) would catch a future `domain/` layer importing it for a color/style constant, which would transitively violate RNF06. No domain code exists yet to violate this, so it's not a bug today — worth a lint rule or architecture test once the first feature's `domain/` layer is scaffolded.
