entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

input.message:
Three parallel review layers (blind-hunter, edge-case-hunter, verification-gap) ran against the diff of your story-1.4 implementation. After triage, the following are classified as "patch" — real, caused by this story, trivially fixable without further human input. Apply all of them, then re-run the spec's Verification section (`fvm flutter pub get`, `fvm flutter test`, `fvm flutter analyze`, the RNF08 grep). Do not touch anything inside `<frozen-after-approval>` in the spec. Pre-existing issues in `auth_cubit.dart` (toggleMode/passwordChanged test gaps) were triaged as "defer" — already logged in deferred-work.md, do NOT fix those here.

1. `lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart` — the `StreamController<SessionStatus>` is never closed. It's a `registerLazySingleton`, and nothing calls `.close()` on it when `resetCoreDependencies()` (`sl.reset()`) runs, leaking it on every test teardown. Add a `dispose()`/`close()` path (e.g. expose a `dispose()` on `SessionRepository`, call it from `resetCoreDependencies()` in `lib/core/di/injection_container.dart`).

2. Same file — `statusStream` is a plain broadcast stream with no "replay last value" semantics: a consumer that subscribes AFTER the first emission (Story 1.5/1.6's future listeners, or any second `StreamBuilder`) gets nothing until the next status change. Give it replay-last-value semantics (seed the current status to new subscribers) so `SessionRepository.statusStream` always reflects current state, not just future changes.

3. `test/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl_test.dart` — the two exception-mapping branches in `restoreSession()` (thrown exception from `readRefreshToken()`, and thrown exception from `saveSession(...)` after a successful refresh) are never tested with a `.thenThrow(...)` stub, unlike the equivalent coverage already present in `auth_repository_impl_test.dart`. Add two tests mirroring that pattern, asserting `Left(MalformedResponse)` + an `unauthenticated` stream emission.

4. `test/core/network/access_token_provider_test.dart` — the new `saveSession`/`readRefreshToken`/`clearSession` methods on `AccessTokenProvider` are never exercised against the real `SecureStorageAccessTokenProvider` impl (only mocks/fakes call them elsewhere). Add round-trip tests following the same faked-native-channel pattern already used in that file for the three pre-existing methods.

5. `test/core/network/network_pipeline_integration_test.dart` — no test proves `auth-refresh` actually goes out over the real pipeline with the anon-key bearer (not a stale/absent access token), the way the existing test already proves for `auth-login`. Add one equivalent case for `auth-refresh`.

6. `test/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl_test.dart` — the "cold boot, no stored session" test only asserts `result.isLeft()`, unlike the sibling "dead refresh token" tests which assert the specific failure type. Strengthen it to assert the specific `Failure` subtype returned.

7. `lib/core/network/access_token_provider.dart` — `saveSession`/`clearSession` each do two independent sequential `_storage.write`/`_storage.delete` calls with no atomicity. If the second call fails after the first succeeds, access and refresh tokens end up mismatched (saveSession) or half-cleared (clearSession). Make each operation either atomic or safely consistent on partial failure (e.g. roll back the first write if the second fails, or write/delete in an order that fails safe).

8. `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/tests/test-summary.md` — has no "Story 1.4" section, even though story 1.3's own section in that same file explicitly promised one ("When story 1.4 lands, extend network_pipeline_integration_test.dart-style coverage... and add the equivalent repository-layer failure matrix"). Add a Story 1.4 section following the established pattern from the 1.2/1.3 sections already in that file.

9. `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-1-4-silent-session-refresh-persistence.md` — the RNF08 Verification grep command scopes `lib/features/auth lib/core/network` but not `lib/main.dart`, which is where this story's actual new UI code (the `StreamBuilder`/blank `Scaffold`) lives. Widen the grep's path list to include `lib/main.dart`.

10. `lib/main.dart` — `unawaited(_sessionRepository.restoreSession())` has no error backstop. Add a trivial `.catchError((_) {})` (or equivalent) as defensive insurance, even though current internal paths are already guarded.

11. `lib/main.dart` — the blank boot `Scaffold` shown while `restoreSession()` is pending has no fallback loading indicator if the call runs long (both `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` and `NETWORK_OFFLINE` are retryable per `RetryInterceptor`, so a slow/offline boot can leave the blank screen for several seconds to tens of seconds with zero feedback — a real RNF01 violation beyond the happy path). Add a indicator that appears only after ~300ms of waiting, consistent with RNF01's existing threshold and this codebase's existing "no new shared-widget param, minimal inline treatment" convention (see how Story 1.3's submit button handles this).

12. `lib/features/auth/data/datasources/auth_remote_data_source.dart` doc comment cites `openapi.yaml:179-234` for `auth-refresh`, while the spec's own Code Map cites `openapi.yaml:179-240` for the same endpoint. Align the doc comment's line range with the spec's.

When done, report what you changed and the fresh verification output (test count, analyze result).

  3. **Missing exception-path tests** — added two tests to `session_repository_impl_test.dart`: `readRefreshToken()` throwing, and `saveSession()` throwing after a successful refresh — both asserting `Left(MalformedResponse)` + an `unauthenticated` emission, mirroring `auth_repository_impl_test.dart`'s existing pattern.   6. **Weak "no stored session" assertion** — that test in `session_repository_impl_test.dart` now also asserts the returned failure is specifically `isA<AuthExpired>()`, matching the sibling dead-token tests' pattern.

  10. **Unawaited `restoreSession()` error backstop** — `main.dart`'s `initState` now does `.catchError(_asUnauthenticated)` before `unawaited(...)`. The handler returns `Either<Failure, Unit>` (not `void`) — a void-returning handler would try to complete the Future with `null`, which isn't assignable to that non-nullable type and would itself throw, defeating the backstop.
  
  11. **No loading feedback on a slow/offline boot** — added a private `_BootLoadingScreen` (StatefulWidget) shown while `statusStream` has no data: blank for the first 300ms (`Timer`), then a centered `CircularProgressIndicator` using `DesignTokens.colorPrimary`. Timer is cancelled in `dispose()`. No new shared-widget param, matching the existing minimal-treatment convention.
  
  12. **Doc-comment line-range mismatch** — `auth_remote_data_source.dart`'s `refresh()` doc comment now cites `openapi.yaml:179-240`, matching the spec's own Code Map citation (was `179-234`).
  
  ## Fresh verification output

  - `fvm flutter analyze` — **No issues found!**
  - `fvm flutter test` — **192/192 passing** (was 184 before this patch round; +8 new tests: 2 exception-path + 1 replay-semantics in `session_repository_impl_test.dart`, 4 round-trip in `access_token_provider_test.dart`, 1 `auth-refresh` case in `network_pipeline_integration_test.dart`).

  ## Scope note on formatting
  
  I ran `fvm dart format` only against the exact files touched in this patch round (explicit file list, not a directory glob) — `git status` confirms no unrelated files were touched this time (learned from the earlier broad-glob mistake in my first pass on this story).
  
  Nothing left incomplete from the 12-item list. The spec's frontmatter `status` now reads `in-review` (I'd left it at `review`; it appears your own review workflow already advanced it further, which I left untouched).
</agent-message>

21	
22	## Boundaries & Constraints
23	
24	**Always:**
25	- Boot calls `auth-refresh` once, unconditionally, whenever a refresh token is stored — no client-side expiry math or clock comparison; the server is the sole source of truth for validity.

29	- `AuthRepositoryImpl._authenticate` (`auth_repository_impl.dart:46-74`) persists the refresh token returned by signup/login too, via the same `saveSession`.
30	- A dead/missing refresh token reuses the closed 14-subtype `Failure` hierarchy (`AuthExpired`/`AuthInvalid`) — no new subtype (`failure.dart`).
31	
32	**Ask First:** if the backend's `auth-refresh` response omits any field `openapi.yaml:197-234` marks required, HALT before guessing a fallback.
33

36	- No `go_router` wiring (Story 1.6) — `main.dart` keeps its current `MaterialApp`/`Navigator` shape; only `home` changes.
37	- No new Cubit for this story — `main.dart` drives directly off `SessionRepository`.

**Approach:** Persist the refresh token; add a `SessionRepository` in the auth domain that, on launch, unconditionally exchanges any stored refresh token for a fresh pair via `auth-refresh`, exposing the result as the epic's one singleton `SessionStatus` stream. `main.dart` branches its `home` on that stream's first emission instead of hardcoding `AuthScreen`.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Boot calls `auth-refresh` once, unconditionally, whenever a refresh token is stored — no client-side expiry math or clock comparison; the server is the sole source of truth for validity.

- Unconditional refresh-at-boot (no client-side expiry math) trades one always-on network round trip for zero clock-skew bugs; revisit only if the 300ms-threshold UX proves this too slow in practice.
- Mid-session reactive refresh-on-401 is deliberately deferred to Story 1.5 (the overlay) rather than solved here with a second mechanism.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter pub get` -- resolves, no conflicts
- `fvm flutter test` -- all tests pass
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- zero issues
- `grep -rn "Color(0x\|fontSize:\|EdgeInsets\.\(all\|symmetric\|only\)(" lib/features/auth lib/core/network lib/main.dart --include=*.dart` -- expected: no matches (RNF08) -- widened to include `lib/main.dart`, where this story's own new UI (the `StreamBuilder`/boot-loading screen) actually lives

lines: - `grep -rn "Color(0x\|fontSize:\|EdgeInsets\.\(all\|symmetric\|only\)(" lib/features/auth lib/core/network lib/main.dart --include=*.dart` -- expected: no matches (RNF08) -- widened to include `lib/main.dart`, where this story's own new UI (the `StreamBuilder`/boot-loading screen) actually lives
+- The one new DI-singleton access point for session validity — a stream plus a one-shot restore call, nothing else.
+- The two-state status the epic's AD requires — no third "expired-mid-session" state, deliberately deferred to Story 1.5.
+- `restoreSession()` — unconditional refresh, no client-side expiry math; the server is the sole source of truth.
+- Only a backend-confirmed dead token clears storage; any other failure leaves it untouched so the next boot retries.
+- Replay-last-value stream: a late subscriber still sees current status immediately, not just future changes.
+- `saveSession`/`clearSession` write the refresh token first — the one field `restoreSession()` actually keys its next-boot decision on.
+- `AuthRepositoryImpl._authenticate` now persists the refresh token too, not just the access token.
+- `auth-refresh`'s own body/response shape can't reuse `_post`/`AuthResponseDto` — decodes the nested `session` object directly.
+- `home` branches on `statusStream` instead of hardcoding `AuthScreen`; `restoreSession()` fires once in `initState`.
+- Blank for the happy path, spinner only past RNF01's 300ms threshold — a slow/offline boot no longer looks frozen.
+- `SessionRepository` registered as a singleton with `dispose:` wired into `get_it`'s own reset lifecycle.
+- The four I/O-matrix rows plus the two exception-mapping paths and the replay-semantics check.
+- Real `SecureStorageAccessTokenProvider` round-trip coverage for the new session methods.
+- `auth-refresh` proven over the real pipeline with the anon-key bearer, mirroring the existing `auth-login` case.
+- Both boot branches (authenticated vs unauthenticated home) driven through the real composition root.

content.text:
Story 1.4 — Silent Session Refresh & Persistence is implemented, reviewed, and committed.

**What was built:**
- `AccessTokenProvider` now persists the refresh token alongside the access token ([access_token_provider.dart](lib/core/network/access_token_provider.dart))
- A new `SessionRepository` (auth domain) exposes the epic's one singleton `SessionStatus` stream — with replay-last-value semantics and proper `dispose()` wiring into `get_it`'s reset lifecycle ([session_repository.dart](lib/features/auth/domain/repositories/session_repository.dart), [session_repository_impl.dart](lib/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl.dart))
- `main.dart` now boots by calling `restoreSession()` and branching its home screen off that stream instead of hardcoding `AuthScreen` — with a 300ms-gated loading indicator for slow/offline boots ([main.dart](lib/main.dart))
- Signup/login now persist the refresh token too ([auth_repository_impl.dart](lib/features/auth/data/repositories/auth_repository_impl.dart))

**Process:** planned → self-reviewed against the Ready-for-Development standard → approved by you → implemented by a subagent → reviewed by three parallel layers (blind-hunter, edge-case-hunter, verification-gap) → 12 real findings classified as auto-fixable patches (stream leak, missing replay semantics, untested exception paths, non-atomic token writes, a genuine RNF01 gap on slow boots, missing test-summary section, etc.) and applied → 2 pre-existing, unrelated findings in `auth_cubit.dart` logged to `deferred-work.md` rather than fixed here.

**Verification (I ran this independently, not just trusting the subagent):** `fvm flutter analyze` — zero issues; `fvm flutter test` — 192/192 passing.

**Commit:** `b9870eb` — scoped to story 1.4's own files only. The pre-existing dirty files from stories 1.2/1.3's uncommitted review patches (`app_button.dart`, `app_text_field.dart`, `avatar.dart`, `auth_cubit.dart` + their tests, `component_library_interaction_test.dart`, the spec-1-2/1-3 markdown files) are still uncommitted, exactly as they were before I started — I left them for you to commit separately since they're unrelated to this story.

The spec file is open in VS Code with a **Suggested Review Order** section — Cmd+click the links there to jump to each review stop in order.
